newsitem.title: USA: Hughes offers consumer satellite Internet access.
newsitem.headline: Hughes offers consumer satellite Internet access.

text.p: Hughes Network Systems said Thursday it is now offering its satellite-based DirecPC Internet access system to consumers.

In a series of announcements, Hughes said it had agreed to licensing deals with leading Internet software and access providers to make the system easy to install and use by consumers. The company is a unit of Hughes Electronics Corp.

The target audience for the DirecPC system will be heavy Internet users. Initially it can be purchased at CompUSA Inc. retail superstores in California, reflecting the concentrated demand for high-speed Internet services in that state.
DirecPC allows users to download information from Internet access at speeds of up to roughly 400,000 bits per second.

The service is 14 times faster than modems connected to standard phone lines at 28,800 bits per second, or Integrated Services Digital Network (ISDN) access that transmits data about four times faster than conventional phone lines.
The DirecPC package retails for about $699 and includes a 21-inch satellite dish, a connecting cable running inside the home, and an adapter card installed inside the customer's PC.

Thursday's announcements mark Hughes' first concerted effort to market the service to consumers, although the system has been passively available at the company's Web site for several months, a spokeswoman said.
DirecPC originally was introduced in April 1995 for companies who use the service largely to create high-speed private computer communication networks.
Hughes said it will bundle Microsoft Corp.'s Internet Explorer and Netscape Communications Corp.'s Navigator as optional browsers with its DirecPC Personal Edition.
The DirecPC service is designed to be equally easy to use with either browser programme, a Hughes official said.
Hughes said it had worked closely with two national Internet providers -- Netcom On-Line Communications Inc. and Earthlink Network Inc. to insure that DirecPC was easy to install and use.
However, the system can work with any access provider a consumer may choose, the company said.
Hughes is a subsidiary of General Motors Corp.
Hughes Electronics shares, which trade as a special class of General Motors stock, fell $1 to $54 on the New York Stock Exchange.
